nodes.name: Red fir
nodes.desc: Dominant conifer of the red fir forest between about 6,500 and 8,000 feet, and a seed source for squirrels.

nodes.name: Whitebark pine
nodes.desc: A hardy high-elevation pine of the subalpine zone. Its large seeds feed Clark's nutcrackers and bears, and nutcrackers spread it by caching seeds.

nodes.name: Ceanothus
nodes.desc: A shrub of the mixed conifer zone that mule deer browse. Many species are adapted to regrow or germinate after fire.

nodes.name: Pinemat manzanita
nodes.desc: A low evergreen shrub whose berries are eaten by Sierra Nevada red foxes when in season.

nodes.name: Lupines & wildflowers
nodes.desc: Lupine and other mountain wildflowers bloom in meadows as the snow melts and feed deer, pikas and ground squirrels.

nodes.name: Mule deer
nodes.desc: Browses shrubs and eats forbs. Cougars, coyotes and bobcats prey on it, and its carcasses feed scavengers.

nodes.name: Clark's nutcracker
nodes.desc: Relies mainly on pine seeds, especially whitebark pine, and buries surplus seeds that can sprout into new trees.

nodes.name: Douglas squirrel
nodes.desc: Eats mainly conifer seeds and stores cones in a midden. Preyed on by martens, bobcats and owls.

nodes.name: Golden-mantled ground squirrel
nodes.desc: The most recorded mammal near the park. An omnivore of pine nuts, plants, fungi and insects that hibernates in winter.

nodes.name: American pika
nodes.desc: A heat-sensitive herbivore of talus slopes that stores cut vegetation in haypiles for winter.

nodes.name: Deer mouse
nodes.desc: A very common small rodent and a meal for foxes, coyotes, snakes and other predators.

nodes.name: Common raven
nodes.desc: A clever omnivore and scavenger that feeds on carrion, small animals and other birds.

nodes.name: Sierra Nevada red fox
nodes.desc: A rare montane fox with a small Lassen population. Its diet is mostly rodents and mule deer, plus birds, insects and manzanita berries.

nodes.name: Coyote
nodes.desc: A flexible predator and scavenger that takes rodents, pikas and deer fawns and feeds on carrion.

nodes.name: Bobcat
nodes.desc: A small cat that hunts squirrels, pikas and rodents and sometimes deer fawns.

nodes.name: American black bear
nodes.desc: Mostly a plant eater (berries, nuts) that also eats insects, fawns and carrion, and raids squirrel nut caches.

nodes.name: Cougar
nodes.desc: The park's top cat. Deer are its main prey, and black bears often take over its kills.

nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Short, bright summers drive plant growth once the snow has gone.

nodes.name: Winter snowpack
nodes.desc: Lake Helen gets roughly 600 to 700 inches a year, and meltwater feeds meadows and forests into summer.

nodes.name: Wildfire
nodes.desc: The 2021 Dixie Fire burned about 69% of the park and opened ground for fire-adapted shrubs.

nodes.name: Volcanic soil
nodes.desc: Soils on volcanic rock supply nutrients to the park's forests and meadows.

nodes.name: Fungi & bacteria
nodes.desc: Break down dead trees, plants and carcasses and return nutrients to the soil.
